text:
An Englishman says he lives with the world’s oldest cat—a tortoiseshell born in 1995, making her 31 years-old.

The puss named Millie was first owned by Leslie Greenhough’s late wife, who took her in as a 3-month-old kitten.

Leslie told SWNS news agency that Millie’s long lifespan is a result of giving her only natural mineral water for the past decade—alongside “lots of treats” and “cuddles on the sofa”.

The family from Greater Manchester celebrated her birthday earlier this year, treating her to a bowl full of chicken.

“I am very proud she has made it to 31,” said the 71-year-old owner. “She is a real trooper.”

Leslie says his ‘life ambition’ is to get her in the Guinness Book of records, but sadly he can’t prove her age.

“Unfortunately, the only person who can do that is my late wife.”

And the only item of proof he has is an image taken in 1995 of Millie eating out of a food bowl his wife took.

A unique story explains how spring water became the cat’s drink of choice.

“Near to our house, work was being done to the water pipes, and because I am old and classified as a vulnerable person—so they began dropping off Buxton bottled water at my doorstep, which I also gave to Millie.

“When I turned my taps back on afterwards, dirty water came out, so I chose to stick with the Buxton, which I have stuck with ever since.

“She only drinks Buxton water—and has a daily diet of salmon, prawns, chicken and tuna.

“Millie is around 146—in human years. I think that says it all really. Imagine being 146 years-old—I can’t.”

“She’s developed a cautious attitude; she’s very shy. I think that’s helped her live longer.”

Millie’s personality has also mellowed with her age, becoming more “relaxed” and “chilled out” around the house.

“My wife would be amazed with how well she is doing.”

She’s needed extra care lately, however, due to the heatwave engulfing the UK.

Millie now has two fans blowing on her, at all times, and ice cubes in her water bowl to keep her cool.

The oldest cat ever confirmed in the world was named Creme Puff, and lived to be 38 years and 3 days old. The oldest feline currently verified living today cat is Flossie from the UK, who is currently 30 years old.
